content: The article discusses the high cost of hiring private consultants by public bodies in the UK. According to the figures from outsourcing data company Tussell, the government's spending on private consultants increased by 62% from 2019-20 to 2023-24, reaching £3.4 billion in the last year. The surge in consultant spending seen during the COVID-19 pandemic has not returned to pre-pandemic levels. The article highlights the challenge facing the new Labour government, which aims to halve the government's spend on consultants during this parliament. The article also mentions a recent £223 million government contract awarded to KPMG to train civil servants, as well as other consultant contracts totaling nearly £650 million that have been awarded since the Labour government took power. The article includes a quote from an academic criticizing the "cult of hiring consultants," arguing that they contribute little value to complex organizations.
